Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment A strong thermal day with sharp lapse rates, high cloud cover, and increasing west/southwest winds. No precipitation or overdevelopment is expected, but terrain-driven rotor and low-level shear will be present at several sites.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury: Favorable — good thermals but SE launch becomes crosswind after mid-morning; best thermal window 10am–2pm, peak w* 440 fpm, thermal ceiling 5451 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (9.7 °C/km) — advanced pilots only.
  • Hallelujah: Favorable — ridge-soarable wind direction much of the day with strong thermals and an evening ridge-soaring option after 7pm; low-level shear present. Window 10am–5pm (evening 7–9pm), peak w* 474 fpm, ceiling 6270 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (9.8 °C/km) — advanced pilots only.
  • Slide Mountain: Unfavorable — strong SW wind crosses the SE launch and high bulk shear (33 mph) severely limits safe flying; brief thermal window 9–11am, peak w* 371 fpm, ceiling 2559 ft AGL.
  • McClellan: Favorable — light winds with strong thermals; wind direction mostly on-spec until mid-afternoon, but low‑level shear aloft (5 mph/layer). Window 10am–3pm, peak w* 527 fpm, ceiling 6062 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (10.0 °C/km) — advanced pilots only.
  • West McClellan: Marginal — thermals are good but wind is cross to the launch until late afternoon when it becomes gusty; window 10am–4pm, peak w* 495 fpm, ceiling 5459 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (9.7 °C/km) — advanced pilots only.
  • Peavine Mountain: Marginal — winds are directionally aligned but strengthen steadily, becoming very strong by late afternoon; best window 9am–1pm, peak w* 466 fpm, ceiling 4341 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (8.6 °C/km) — advanced pilots only.
  • Rainbow Ridge: Favorable — excellent morning ridge and thermal soaring with the highest ceiling of the day; wind shifts off-direction in the afternoon and high‑altitude shear (8 mph/layer) is a hazard. Window 9am–1pm, peak w* 512 fpm, ceiling 7647 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (10.1 °C/km) — advanced pilots only.
  • Duck Hill: Marginal — ridge-soaring wind direction is rarely within spec and strong afternoon winds develop; use a brief thermal window 10am–2pm, peak w* 508 fpm, ceiling 7194 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (9.9 °C/km) — advanced pilots only.
  • Daydreams: Marginal — weak thermals and gusty afternoon winds limit the ridge-soaring window; best window 8am–1pm, peak w* 176 fpm, ceiling 3150 ft AGL. Sharp thermals (8.6 °C/km) — advanced pilots only.

Hazards

  • Sharp thermals: Lapse rates of 8.6–10.1 °C/km at all sites except Slide Mountain — suitable for advanced/expert pilots only.
  • Low-level wind shear: Hazardous layer speed shear (≥5 mph/layer) at Hallelujah, Slide Mountain, McClellan, Rainbow Ridge, and Duck Hill.
  • Rotor/lee turbulence: Increasing W/SW flow will generate rotor and mechanical turbulence downwind of Peavine Mountain and the Carson Range ridgelines.
  • Strong afternoon winds: Peak gusts of 23–32 mph at Kingsbury, Slide, Peavine, and Duck Hill after mid-afternoon — crosswind and gusty conditions for most launches.
  • Icing potential: Cloud base can reach 9,120 ft AGL (site max) while the freezing level is 14,250 ft MSL; pilots climbing near cloud base risk airframe icing.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
